subject: Task 20.2 — F7 coverage tests (Phase 20, Goal F7, ADR-024) test suite

findings.description: The absent-baseline leg is proven for the fresh restoration but not for the restart resume, while the phase-level acceptance wording covers both. AbsentBaselineRestorationRemovesTheArrtagsImageWithoutSaveOrUpdate drives a complete absent-baseline removal and CoordinatorDrivenRestorationIsResumedByTheOrdinaryRecoveryGate drives a complete present-baseline resume, but no test resumes a Restoration whose CandidateAfterPresence is Absent. PLANS.md's Phase 20 acceptance criterion reads that an owned empty selection 'restores the baseline, or removes the ArrTags image when the baseline was absent, through the crash-recoverable protocol and the internal ArtworkPublisher.RestoreAsync entry point (resumed on restart by the ordinary recovery gate)', and ADR-024 clause 3 says a Normal-fence restoration 'is resumed on restart' without restricting that to a present baseline. The impact is bounded: ResumeRestorationAsync is the same entry for both and only skips the artifact read when SourcePresence is Absent, then hands off to the shared ExecuteRestorationAsync whose absent branch the direct-publisher test now pins, so the resume path for an absent baseline is covered by shared code rather than by a dedicated case. What is not covered is a regression confined to the resume entry itself for an absent candidate. This is recorded against the phase wording, not against task 20.2, whose own criterion 4 (worker-report.json acceptance_criteria[3]) asks only for 'a Restoration ArtworkOperation created under the Normal fence' to be resumed, which the test satisfies; docs/architecture/09 and the F7 register wording are already assigned to task 20.3.

findings.description: The reflection helper used by the three direct-publisher tests is deterministic and fail-loud, and it hides nothing behaviorally. typeof(ArtworkPublisher).GetMethod("RestoreAsync", BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.NonPublic) resolves the single internal overload, Assert.NotNull(method) prevents a silent no-op if the method is renamed or removed, and the invocation passes the same instance and the same arguments a production caller passes, so nothing about the removal behavior is substituted. The only cost is coupling: a rename becomes a runtime Assert failure and a second overload becomes an AmbiguousMatchException instead of a compile error, and the cast to Task<ArtworkReconciliationResult> would fail loudly on a signature change. No assertion is weakened by the indirection. Recorded from the determinism/isolation angle; the same mechanism is already recorded by the implementation review as AR-20.2-01.

findings.description: Two assertions in the new result test are restatements rather than independent guarantees, and one new fact duplicates a theory row; recorded so they are not later counted as extra independent proof. (a) The theory asserts Preserved == (reconciliationOutcome != Completed), but Preserved is defined as Outcome is not (Published or Restored), so once the outcome mapping is asserted the Preserved assertion follows by construction; it pins the intended relationship rather than an independent one. (b) RefusedRestorationKeepsTheRenderPassThroughClassification asserts the same outcome, the same retained NoDisplayableValue reason, and the same preserved flag as the NothingToReconcile row of FromRestorationMapsTheBoundedReconciliationOutcome, differing only in the reason text, which is not asserted to a constant. (c) The theory covers the six members TQR-20.1-04 enumerated; the remaining ArtworkReconciliationOutcome members (Resumed, Aborted, CommittedFinalState, ItemRemoved, Deferred) still reach the default arm untested, which is inside the scoped gap but worth stating. None of this creates false confidence: the mapping itself is sensitive, and I changed NothingToReconcile to Blocked (the theory row and the duplicate fact both failed) and changed the default arm to Published (exactly the three blocked rows failed).

substitutes_checked: FakeArtworkHost in ArtworkPublisherTests stands in for the Jellyfin image writer, but it does not hide the behavior under test: RemoveCalls is counted, RemoveImageAsync nulls CurrentBytes, SaveCalls/UpdateCalls are counted separately, and PhaseProbe re-reads the durable ArtworkOperation from the real ArtworkOperationStore at the moment RemoveImageAsync is entered, so Assert.Equal(MutationStarted, _host.PhaseAtRemove) proves write-ahead ordering against the real journal rather than a stub. The real host image-mutation ABI itself stays host-guarded and was not run here.

The reflection helper in the three direct-publisher tests bypasses only the production visibility boundary (internal, per ADR-024 clause 2). It resolves the single internal overload on the same instance with the same arguments, Assert.NotNull prevents a silent no-op, and no production file changed.

FakeRenderer (ArtworkGenerationCoordinatorTests) and the new PassThroughRenderer (ArtworkReconcilerTests) inject the pass-through reason instead of rendering. The discriminator seam is closed on the real renderer by the pre-existing unguarded RendererBehaviorFailureTests rows and by the new native coordinator case, and the crash-recovery case makes no claim about rendering: it asserts renderer.Calls == 1 before the restart, so a resume that re-rendered could not pass.

The synthetic persisted states in the new tests are built through the real PublishedArtworkStateTransitions.CaptureSession/CommitPublication and the real SourceArtifactStore, not hand-assembled records, so the absent-baseline and owned-session states the publisher validates are genuine production transitions. PublishedStateWithActive matches the fake host's reported bytes because the shared ownership comparer would otherwise report a change.
RendererBehaviorFixtures.CreateOpaquePng in the native case is a real SKBitmap encode and a real decode, not a stub; that is precisely why the case is native-guarded.
skips_checked: The single new skip is NonFittingSelectionOnAnOwnedSessionPassesThroughAsNoFittingBadgeWithoutMutation, guarded by SkiaNativeFactAttribute (tests/ArrTags.Tests/SkiaHostCompatibilityTests.cs:141-153). The guard is a genuine environment requirement: the case needs libSkiaSharp to encode the SKBitmap and to decode the source inside SkiaBadgeRenderer, plus the transitive libfontconfig, exactly like the class's pre-existing decode-dependent siblings. It is guarded consistently with them, not uniquely.

The skip is reported, not hidden: the default run prints the case as an explicit [SKIP] line, the default skip count rose from the re-measured 65 to 66, and nothing in the default suite claims to verify the NoFittingBadge guarantee on the strength of the skip (the default-configuration proof is the 20.1 FakeRenderer theory row).
Under the guard the case genuinely executes: the focused pinned-oracle run is 1 passed / 0 skipped, and the full forced-native suite at 2013/21/2034 includes it.

The 20 ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR host facts and the 1 ARRTAGS_NONCANONICAL_GOLDENS comparison skip in every configuration here because the pinned host is absent; they are unrelated to 20.2 and no ADR-024 deliverable is counted against them.
The host-guarded leg was not run and is reported as unverified rather than passed.
determinism_checked: Per-test isolation: each ArtworkGenerationCoordinatorTests and ArtworkReconcilerTests instance creates its own GUID-suffixed temp root, its own StateRepository, stores, publisher, coordinator, reconciler, host and renderer, and deletes the root on Dispose. No static mutable state is introduced; the static Item/Surface/At fields are read-only, and the new static Identity helper in ArtworkGenerationCoordinatorTests and the instance helpers in the other two files allocate fresh values.

No cross-class subject-gate contention was added: ArtworkReconcilerTests uses a per-instance Guid item (including the new restart case), and the coordinator tests reuse the class's pre-existing fixed RenderTestFixtures.ItemId exactly as the pre-existing tests do. The static ArtworkSubjectGate semaphores only serialize; they cannot change an outcome, and the three repeated focused runs and both full-suite runs produced identical counts.

The simulated restart is genuine and deterministic: the interrupted save throws before SaveCalls is incremented, the exception is not an OperationCanceledException so it is contained by RestoreAsync's bounded catch which persists nothing, and the test then builds a fresh StateRepository, SourceArtifactStore, PublishedArtworkStateStore, ArtworkOperationStore, ArtworkPublisher and ArtworkReconciler over the same root. Every store read hits disk, so nothing of the interrupted attempt is carried in memory. The test is honest that this is a durable-record reconstruction, not a process kill.

ThrowOnSaveOnce is a self-clearing single-shot flag on the per-test fake host, so the interrupted save happens exactly once and the resumed save sees a working host; there is no timing or retry dependence.

No wall-clock, network, or process-state dependence: the new tests use fixed timestamps (DateTimeOffset.UnixEpoch.AddDays(1)) and the production DateTimeOffset.UtcNow stamps are never read by an assertion. The durable record the invalid-fence case corrupts is created by writing raw bytes to the authoritative path, which is deterministic, and the store's fail-closed Invalid result is a pure function of those bytes.

The reflection helper is fail-loud rather than silently skipping: a missing method trips Assert.NotNull, an added overload throws AmbiguousMatchException, and a changed signature fails the Task<ArtworkReconciliationResult> cast. None of those can produce a green test that asserts nothing.

The native NoFittingBadge case is deterministic by construction rather than incidentally passing: at 10x10 the effective scale is clamped so the outer inset consumes the safe area, the safe width and height are non-positive, the status pill cannot be built and the technical values are never packed, so the empty layout is reached with no text measurement and no dependence on fontconfig or the probe sysroot's font set. It also matches the pre-existing 20.1 renderer-level construction, and I reproduced 1/1 under the oracle.

Isolation of the assertions is verified by targeted sensitivity probes rather than by reading, each performed in a throwaway copy under /tmp/final-review/test-quality and reverted afterwards (the repository's git diff src/ is empty and no test file was modified by this audit).
sensitivity_probes_run: Probe A (replacing the absent-baseline branch in ExecuteRestorationAsync with an unconditional SaveImageAsync): only AbsentBaselineRestorationRemovesTheArrtagsImageWithoutSaveOrUpdate failed, with Expected Completed / Actual RecoveryBlocked; EmptySelectionOnAnOwnedSessionRestoresTheRetainedBaseline and CoordinatorDrivenRestorationIsResumedByTheOrdinaryRecoveryGate still passed (Failed 1, Passed 46, Total 47). The removal test therefore proves the removal boundary rather than a save, and isolates it.

Probe A' (the inverse: replacing the branch with an unconditional RemoveImageAsync): 8 cases failed, including EmptySelectionOnAnOwnedSessionRestoresTheRetainedBaseline and MissingFenceStoreDrivesTheRestoreUnderTheNormalFence, so the present-baseline restore is pinned to the save boundary by the new RemoveCalls == 0 assertion as well as by the byte and call-count assertions.

Probe B (ResumeRecoveryAsync's restoration branch changed from Restoration to Publication): CoordinatorDrivenRestorationIsResumedByTheOrdinaryRecoveryGate failed with Expected Completed / Actual RecoveryBlocked (plus the six pre-existing recovery cases), so the resume test genuinely exercises the restoration resume branch rather than passing on a generic recovery path.

Probe C (the coordinator's null-fence-store default changed from Normal to Invalid): only MissingFenceStoreDrivesTheRestoreUnderTheNormalFence and the restart case failed; the fence-store-backed 20.1 restore case still passed, so the new case isolates the null-store default and closes TQR-20.1-01.

Probe D (the coordinator refusal condition changed to fenceState.IsValid && !fenceState.AllowsNewRestoration): only InvalidFenceRecordPreservesAnOwnedSessionWithoutMutation failed (Expected RenderPassThrough / Actual Restored) while the 20.1 ItemRemoved case still passed, so the new case isolates the fail-closed invalid-record guard.

Probe E (ArtworkOperationFencing.AllowsNewRestoration narrowed to Normal only): exactly the four new fence-permitted cases failed (coordinator and publisher theories for Disable and Uninstall), so the permitted legs are sensitive to the production decision and are not restatements of it.
Probe F (the two FromRestoration mapping mutations described in TQR-20.2-05): each failed exactly the intended rows.
summary: The 20.2 tests genuinely establish the ADR-024 behaviors 20.2 owns, and every claim in the worker and implementation-reviewer reports is backed by a test I could break. I reproduced the numbers independently: the default suite at 1926/66/1992, the pinned-native forced-native suite at 2013/21/2034, the focused four-class run at 91/1/92 three times, the new native case at 1/1 under the oracle, and the pre-change baseline at 1908/65/1973 on a copy with the four test files reverted to HEAD. That last measurement matters twice: it proves the +19 total is exactly the 19 new cases, so no pre-existing test was dropped, and it makes the +1 skip honest. On meaningfulness, the direct-publisher absent-baseline test is the strongest addition: it pins the removal boundary from both directions (replacing removal with a save fails it; replacing the save with a removal fails eight cases including the strengthened present-baseline restore), it proves write-ahead ordering by re-reading the real durable journal at the moment RemoveImageAsync is entered, and it asserts the save and item-update APIs are never touched. The crash-recovery case asserts the durable artifacts a restart would read (RestorePending, non-terminal Restoration, zero completed mutations, renderer called once) and then genuinely drives ArtworkRecoveryDecisions through the ordinary recovery gate to Completed with the same OperationId; my probe confirms it fails when the restoration resume branch is disabled, and I confirmed the durable Root reconstruction reads from disk. The fence-variant tests are sensitive in both directions (permitted legs fail when AllowsNewRestoration is narrowed; the invalid-record case fails when the coordinator drops IsValid, while the 20.1 ItemRemoved case still passes). The missing-fence-store case isolates the null default. The FromRestoration theory fails on each arm when the arm is mutated. The one new skip is guarded on a real requirement, is reported as an explicit [SKIP], and executes under the pinned oracle. git diff src/ is empty and the test diffs are pure additions, so nothing was weakened to make something pass. Six of the 20.1 TQR gaps assigned to 20.2 are closed as scoped; the only open item is LOW and is about wording rather than a defect — the absent-baseline removal is proven for the fresh restoration but not for the restart resume, while the Phase 20 acceptance criterion reads as though both are resumed, so either 20.3 narrows that wording or one reconciler case seeds an absent-candidate Restoration. No BLOCKER or HIGH finding: the suite cannot pass while the shipped ADR-024 behavior is broken, and nothing is claimed verified in the default configuration that only the forced-native configuration establishes. PASS_WITH_FINDINGS. No test or implementation file was modified by this audit; this report is the only file written, and the orchestrator still owes the state.json reports-array step under docs/agent-contracts.md clause 5.
